utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. As mentioned yesterday, we want to start today by asking the parties whether or not, after having reopened the case and having now immediately heard the case number, the question: Are there any additional exhibits to be tendered? May we first hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the first on his feet yesterday was Mr. Koumjian. What about new exhibits to be tendered from your side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We don't intend to tender any exhibits during the closing arguments. We have no further exhibits other than -- to add to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's my understanding that you withdraw that what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's correct. On reflection, I withdraw that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have any new exhibits, Your Honour. Only we saw yesterday the photocopy of Dr. Stakic's ID card, and it's photocopied only on a page with a picture. And this document is probably we think with OLAD, office of legal aid and detention of this Tribunal. So maybe it would be wise to photocopy the cover page as well from which it is obvious it is a regular ID card. So it wouldn't be a new document, only cover page of the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it contested or can we regard it as an agreed fact that this what we have before us was, in fact, the ID? May I ask the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's not an issue with us. We don't contest it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we do not have any further requests for new documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then this 150th day of the case, we have the first of the agreed facts. Thank you. But to be serious, before we then go to the Status Conference, two issues: We are aware of the problem that in this Tribunal, no doubt being under an adversarial system, and therefore it's for the parties to present the documents, but there seems to be more and more an asymetric procedure. And with some concern, also the Bench found out that it's not without problem that we have Kozarski Vjesnik available for only one part of time. Asymetric in criminal procedures, this is normally nothing very specific. Normally it is mutually asymetric. Asymetric, why? Because on the one-hand side, normally when there is a good contact between Defence counsel and the accused, the Defence as a team knows best what happened and how to get access to the one or other necessary document. They have in all likelihood the best access to these documents, and without going into further details, I just want to mention the word "health centre." On the other hand, we see with far more concern that apparently, and this is special for this Tribunal, the principle of equality of arms tends to be infringed. One can't say that it's already de facto infringed. I think in this case during the last year, both the Defence and the Bench did whatever possible to get the necessary documents and ordered the production of documents also under Rule 98. But under this concrete case and the prevailing circumstances, and knowing that we several times asked for the production of all the remaining Kozarski Vjesnik articles available for the Prosecution, we hereby order the Prosecution under Rule 98 to produce and to make an additional search in the database - this is the real problem, that this database is available only for one party - to conduct a new search whether or not additional Kozarski Vjesnik articles, especially for the time covered by the fourth amended indictment are available. And if so, we order to produce these documents together with a translation no later than the 28th of April this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Frankly, I think this creates a tremendous problem. We have -- I'm not sure of the number of issues, but we have huge quantities of Kozarski Vjesnik in-house. Only a small portion, to my understanding, is translated. I'm not -- because I don't read the language myself, I usually only read the translation. But we can see from some of the photocopies that the newspaper is several or many pages long, and only selective articles have ever been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until now, the understanding was that only -- that Kozarski Vjesnik only in part was available from the database until a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to clarify what we did in this case, the Defence made a request to review Kozarski Vjesnik beyond what had been disclosed under Rule 68 and what had been disclosed under our 65 ter list, and we agreed to make it available for them to come in-house and review those. Frankly, it took a long time for the Defence investigators to come to us and to say "We're ready to look at those articles." I believe two Defence investigators came and spent two days reviewing - and I just went by briefly, but they were in a room with stacks and stacks of newspapers. The OTP -- I do not have -- I can get back to Your Honour with a further report on exactly what is in-house because I don't have those statistics and what the burden would be. But my impression from seeing that stack of documents that the Defence investigators were going through is that there are probably thousands of pages, at least hundreds of pages of material that is not translated that probably deals with things like football games, the weather, and the various events that every local newspaper would cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So can you tell us exactly when it was that Defence counsel or investigators had the chance and opportunity to review Kozarski Vjesnik articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I can try to get the date, but as I recall, we agreed to that quite early in the case, but it took a long time for the Defence investigators to show up and say that they were ready to review them. They spent at least two days in-house. We had to have an investigator sit nearby because some of these are evidence. And they were left in the room with stacks and stacks of newspapers to go through. And the Defence did, I believe, identify several documents which they added to their 65 ter list from that stack of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you clarify, please, until which concrete date in time you have Kozarski Vjesnik available in this premises. Could this be done during the day, this day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the question is when did they review it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. Until when you have Kozarski Vjesnik available? My understanding until now was that only for a limited time you had the editions of Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is my understanding. I'll have to check. It's rather complicated because the Kozarski Vjesnik came from various sources, and I believe, for example, as was testified to by one of the witnesses, he received his copies through a third party from the Soros centre in Sarajevo. And there have been researchers from the Tribunal that have gone to the Soros centre, and that's been available -- we made Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that clear -- that came out in evidence months ago that the Soros foundation in Sarajevo has copies of Kozarski Vjesnik that we don't. That, of course, would be available to the Defence equally as to us. Then there were Kozarski Vjesniks that were seized. Witnesses have occasional brought in, as the Court has seen, copies of Kozarski Vjesnik. So they come from a wide, wide variety of sources, and I know that we had a lot of trouble tracking down all the in-house copies for the Defence, and we did find out at one point that some were missing. We went back and looked again. We found those because they were in a different part of the Tribunal. Frankly, they are being used constantly by different teams. They are reviewing them. So it's a huge problem. But I believe the Defence can verify that their investigators spent at least two days reviewing the issues -- all the issues that we identified we had in-house from the indictment period and I believe going on through 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the Defence on this having complained yesterday about the limited access of Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understood your questions differently than my learned friend answered it. The problem is that our investigators did search the issues of Kozarski Vjesnik, but only the issues they were offered. I think that during this trial, we established that issues from April, May, June, July, August are missing. We were never given the access to these issues from the critical period. When we addressed Kozarski Vjesnik, we were informed that all the issue, especially the issues from this period, were taken by SFOR. Where did they end up? We don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this was exactly my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have different information. I wasn't personally involved. But my information was that the issues from 1992 that we had were given. One -- I just received a message from someone who has done some of the translating and is familiar and they indicate that we do have in-house 1991 through 1995, almost most of the issues, more or less complete. There are approximately 10 from 1992 missing. That would be ten weeks because I believe it's a weekly newspaper. But these have been -- I can double check, but my understanding is that these were provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If my learned friend could clarify which weeks are missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this will be now a difficult exercise. Therefore, we stay with this and would request the Prosecution to grant access and to review once again the issues of Kozarski Vjesnik as the Defence indicated, that there would be prejudice emanating from this having not had access to the issues from April, May, June, July, and August. And I think this can be resolved in this way, that those issues from April, May, June, July, August are to be made available for the Defence and then they may be produced in English also in case the Defence or the Prosecution identifies that the one or other article is relevant for our case. Because to be honest, I don't hate nothing more than judging on a limited base of facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, we believe we have provided to the Defence access to all of the articles from the -- we believe we have provided to the Defence access to all of the articles from the indictment period that was requested. I don't know if the Defence kept a record of the issues that they reviewed. I will check to see what records we have of issues that were provided. There are approximately ten issues missing, as I've stated. But it's our belief, and certainly was our effort, and I can confirm what records we do have by the afternoon, that all the were made available to the Defence investigators who speak the language, read the language, for review. In fact, they have selected several of those articles which they presented during the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I know it's a late stage during the case, but could we agree that under these exceptional circumstances, the Defence would contact the OTP during the break and when these issues from April through August, and if I can count correctly, it may be to a maximum 20 issues, then go through these issues that we have clarified this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Does the OTP agree with this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, and we would appreciate if the Defence kept records of what they reviewed or what they say is missing, we can check and see. That would be very easy to identify if they have a date that's missing, we can easily check our database to see whether it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. I think the case should not conclude with any problems related to prejudice to the one or other party. So I expect that we hear the results immediately after the lunch break. Then two additional points: No doubt that we had it in another case just recently, there is the ongoing obligation under Rule 68 to provide material until the judgement will be handed down in this case. That's point number one. Point number two is that we were confronted with problems in several appeal cases, and there was a complaint by the group of auditors that additional evidence or in a one concrete case, even a deluge of additional evidence was presented under 115 during appeal only. I think when we read our rules on procedure and evidence together, it's quite clear that the intention is to have evidence as soon as possible available for the parties. And it would be a no-go to hand down a judgement knowing that additional evidence is available that would show the case in an entirely different light. So therefore, we yesterday came to the conclusion that we order both parties to apply by motion to present additional evidence before the Trial Chamber, if necessary, if urgent and if of major importance. Such motion shall clarify -- shall clearly identify with precision the specific finding of fact or the points addressed during the case in the Trial Chamber to which the additional evidence is directed and must be served on the other party and filed with the Registrar immediately, immediately, so that it's available for this concrete judgement in order to avoid that an appeal be based on the mere question that additional evidence was available in the time during -- between the closing arguments and the handing down of the judgement. So of course we can't order the Defence to present evidence if it's not in the interest of the client. That goes without saying. That's a principle of the prohibition of self-incrimination. But to put it in a more -- or in a less judicial way, if any of the parties should identify the smoking gun or this could also happen, the peace pipe, please let us know immediately that we can include these facts in our judgement. Our intention is to hand down the judgement somewhere in July, in all likelihood very, very close to the summer court recess. We can't promise anything at this point in time because as it was emphasised by the parties, that no doubt it's a difficult case, difficult related to the facts and difficult related to the law. We take it that those points that were not addressed during the closing arguments until now and that were contained in our questionnaire, or better, the guidance on issues to be addressed in final briefs and/or closing arguments, that the instructions given by the Court will be followed in the final briefs that we can come to better solutions and that we have answers to the open questions identified until now. And we will only come back to these issues in a very, very limited way today. Before we necessarily have to make a short break for the purpose of a Status Conference, may I ask the parties whether or not there are any additional remarks to be made on procedural issues before we start the rebuttal and rejoinder?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have anything, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is not the case. Then for the moment, there would be nothing special. May I ask the parties, what is the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. envisaged time you would need for your rebuttal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would guess about 90 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's premature to ask the Defence, but at this point in time, what is your time estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 45 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course, with the caveat, it depends on what you hear from the Prosecution. Then finally that we are prepared for today's session, may I ask, is there already a decision taken by Dr. Stakic whether or not he wants to make use of his right to give us the last word and thereby his personal impression and assessment of that what has been heard during the last year, also in order to give us an additional access to the personality of Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Dr. Stakic would like to give a short statement and address the Court at the conclusion of the rejoinder and rebuttal portions of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then immediately before the case will be declared closed, we'll do this. Then it remains only for me to announce now a break of about 3 or 4 minutes. We stay tuned, or better sit by in front of the courtroom and let us know when we can restart with a very brief Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be followed by a Status Conference. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.04 a.m.,
